keywords.rule: Counts are papers whose title or abstract contains one of the keyword's phrases (porter-stemmed, as the theme trends); the baseline is the papers in scope first submitted in the 12 weeks before the issue, its own papers excluded. new: fewer than 5 baseline papers; rising: at least 5 papers and a rate at least 1.5 times the baseline rate; hot: at least 15 papers (and 1% of the issue) at a rate at least 0.67 times the baseline rate; steady: otherwise.
keywords.score: log2(1 + n) · log2(1 + (n + 3) / (E + 3)), E = issue papers × (baseline papers with the phrase + 0.5) / baseline papers

themes.name: world models and VLA for embodied AI
themes.summary: These papers develop vision-language-action and world action models for embodied agents, spanning robot skill learning, mobile manipulation, and navigation, with several emphasizing sim-to-real transfer from synthetic data or compact learned future representations. Others address physical realities of embodiment, such as characterizing cloth manipulation variability, calibrating dexterous teleoperation, designing informative trajectories for system identification, and robust navigation under disturbances. They differ in whether they prioritize world modeling, reactive closed-loop control, sim-to-real identification, or perception and calibration.

themes.name: learning theory, optimization, and neural network theory
themes.summary: The papers in this theme develop theoretical and algorithmic analyses of learning, optimization, and neural network representations. They span information-theoretic guarantees for VC learning, ranking from heterogeneous pairwise comparisons, compression perspectives on language modeling, sampling methods for non-smooth heavy-tailed targets, and regret bounds in constrained adversarial MDPs. Other contributions address representational and architectural questions, including implicit neural representations, mixture-of-experts routing, Koopman spectral reliability for dynamical-system learning, federated linear stochastic approximation, and Bayesian shape optimisation.

themes.name: AI for science, medicine, and scientific discovery
themes.summary: The papers apply AI and machine learning across scientific domains including Earth science, materials, chemistry, biology, and medicine. They differ in focus: some develop specialized architectures like neural operators or product-of-experts for physical simulation and multimodal fusion, while others build autonomous agents for experimental design or medical diagnosis. A common thread is addressing domain-specific challenges such as information asymmetry, missing modalities, physical constraints, and cost-aware sequential decision making.

themes.name: evaluation, benchmarking, and auditing of AI systems
themes.summary: The papers in this theme develop benchmarks, auditing frameworks, and evaluation methods for assessing AI systems across diverse domains, including enterprise data synthesis, machine translation, UI design, and theoretical problem-solving. They differ in their specific targets, such as separating evidence-driven revision from pressure-induced shifts in LLMs, attributing failures in multi-agent systems, or measuring persona fidelity in user simulators, while commonly questioning assumed ground truths and model reliability.

themes.name: multimodal vision-language and audio understanding
themes.summary: These papers advance multimodal understanding across vision-language, video, and speech by addressing reliability issues such as hallucination, attention collapse, and insufficient evidence selection, while others tackle cross-modal disentanglement, sign language translation, egocentric spoken assistance, and phonologically informed or paralinguistically disentangled speech modeling. They differ in focus and method, spanning latent reasoning, adversarial and sparse-autoencoder disentanglement, retrieval augmentation, inference-time representation repair, and tokenization for recognition. Together they push toward more grounded, controllable, and semantically precise multimodal systems.

themes.name: AI safety, alignment, privacy, and trustworthiness
themes.summary: The papers address AI safety, alignment, privacy, and trustworthiness from diverse angles, including monitoring deployed models with activation probes, aligning safety across recurrent depths in looped language models, bypassing multi-scanner guardrails, rejection attacks on speculative decoding, distillation for incrimination, identity verification for probabilistic models, adversarial augmentation for face synthesis, state-aware manipulation in federated reinforcement learning, minimax Gaussian mechanisms for continual machine unlearning, guard models for unfulfilled obligations, world models as verifiers for GUI agents, and a persistent accuracy ceiling in automated verbal deception detection. They differ in their specific threat models and defense mechanisms, ranging from attack techniques to privacy-preserving algorithms and evaluation studies.

themes.name: diffusion and flow-matching generative modeling
themes.summary: The papers in this theme advance diffusion and flow-matching generative modeling by improving inference efficiency, theoretical understanding, and application-specific generation. They differ in focus, ranging from spectral feature caching and quantization for diffusion transformers to optimal transport and quantum circuit execution for flow models, as well as domain applications like eyeglass reflection removal and weather nowcasting.

themes.name: efficient LLM inference and context management
themes.summary: The papers address efficient LLM inference and context management by curating or compressing context, reusing and compressing KV caches, and designing specialized memory architectures for agents. They differ in whether they focus on agent memory curation and forgetting, long-term dialogue memory with graph augmentation, or inference optimizations such as cross-model KV-cache reuse, low-bit quantization, and sparse Mixture-of-Experts routing.

themes.name: time series, tabular, and structured data modeling
themes.summary: Papers in this theme develop models and frameworks for time series, tabular, and structured data, addressing challenges like forecasting, tabular prediction, semantic table interpretation, and anomaly detection. They differ in focus: some propose foundation models and test-time adaptation for time series forecasting, others target tabular in-context learning and foundation models, while others handle graph-structured data or metadata-only table interpretation. Common threads include handling missing or noisy data, structured decoding, and leveraging pretrained models.

themes.name: 3D vision, Gaussian splatting, and spatial perception
themes.summary: The papers in this theme advance three-dimensional scene representation and spatial perception, with a strong focus on Gaussian splatting variants for reconstruction, evaluation, and appearance modeling. They also address robustness in dynamic or resource-constrained settings, such as multi-robot localization, loss-resilient collaborative perception, and event-camera localization against LiDAR maps. Differences lie in their target problems—ranging from physics-fidelity benchmarking and geometry-aware regularization to cross-time-of-day rendering and explainable three-dimensional disentanglement—and in their methodological emphasis on memory, attention, or confidence weighting.

themes.name: reinforcement learning for LLM reasoning and post-training
themes.summary: These papers investigate post-training and reinforcement learning techniques for improving reasoning in large language models, spanning on-policy distillation, knowledge distillation, GRPO variants, calibration, and test-time training. They differ in whether they modify the rollout process, use offline versus on-policy student data, address entropy collapse, or add verifier-guided inference-time intervention and hindsight-based planning.

themes.name: agentic coding and software engineering agents
themes.summary: These papers study LLM-based coding agents and agentic workflows applied across software engineering, spanning requirements engineering, formal specification generation, code generation and debugging, program evolution, and evaluation of local agents. Many propose multi-agent or self-refining frameworks that use execution feedback, trajectory-guided fault localization, or software-history experience to improve agent behavior. They differ in target and evaluation: some build benchmarks for long-horizon, multi-turn, closed-loop, embedded, or data-engineering settings, while others probe reliability concerns such as overconfident failures, conflicting co-installed skills, and overconfidence in generated code.

highlights.title: Real Long-Term Memory for AI: A 50-Million-Token Window That Is Faster and Cheaper Than Recompute
highlights.theme: efficient LLM inference and context management
highlights.why: Demonstrates byte-exact KV cache reuse from NVMe across a 50M-token window with speed/energy gains, strongly applicable to long-context serving.
highlights.key_result: The paper reports a 50,000,000-token memory layer that restored all probed blocks from encrypted local NVMe storage without recompute (100 of 100, at depths from 0 to 50M tokens) for both Gemma 4 12B and Gemma 4 31B, with constant GPU memory. Compared with recompute, restore was 2.8 to 4.3 faster and used 8.8 to 12.3 less GPU energy, and the 12B model answered 82/100 and the 31B model 98/100 with zero hallucinations.
evidence: We describe a memory layer, released as the public package galahad-kv, that removes both restrictions for a served model, and we report measurements of it on a corpus of 50,000,000 tokens. The layer writes the KV state that the model computes for each block of 16,000 tokens to encrypted local NVMe storage and can later restore any block byte-exact, with zero recompute and at constant GPU memory. In our experiment the corpus consisted of real public text and the model was served through vLLM on one NVIDIA H100. All probed blocks were restored from the encrypted store without recompute (100 of 100, at depths from 0 to 50M tokens) for both Gemma 4 12B and Gemma 4 31B. Compared with recomputing the same block, a restore was 2.8 to 4.3 faster and consumed 8.8 to 12.3 less GPU energy, while GPU memory remained flat over the entire 50M-token stream. When asked about facts planted millions of tokens earlier, the 12B model answered 82/100 correctly and the 31B model 98/100, with zero hallucinations on either.

highlights.title: Velocity Scaling in Flow Matching
highlights.why: Corrects the prior velocity-magnitude deficit explanation for flow matching scaling and identifies population time lag, enabling large FID improvements.
highlights.key_result: We show that MSE training does not create a velocity-magnitude deficit. We find instead that velocity scaling reduces population time lag, and measuring population time lag and using it to select a gain greatly improves generation quality, reducing FID from 28.0 to 12.2 on ImageNet-256 at NFE 25 without guidance.
evidence: We show that MSE training does not create a velocity-magnitude deficit. We find instead that velocity scaling reduces population time lag: sampled states at model time t resemble training states from an earlier time. Velocity scaling and moving model time back are two ways to address this population time lag. Across architectures and model sizes, measuring population time lag and using it to select a gain greatly improves generation quality, reducing FID from 28.0 to 12.2 Estimated by linear interpolation between FID measurements at neighboring gains. on ImageNet-256 at NFE 25 without guidance.

highlights.title: Cross-Embodiment Robot Foundation World Models with Latent Actions
highlights.authors: Huang Huang, Sriram Yenamandra, Arjun Majumdar et al.
highlights.theme: world models and VLA for embodied AI
highlights.why: Presents a cross-embodiment world model with a learned unified latent action space that scales positively with pretraining embodiments, addressing a core generalization challenge.
highlights.key_result: LAC-WM improves downstream performance over EAC-WM by up to 46.7% on dexterous manipulation and 11.7% on LIBERO, and the unified latent action space allows LAC-WM's downstream performance to scale positively with the number of embodiments used during pretraining.
evidence: We evaluate both models on dexterous manipulation tasks and a modified LIBERO benchmark. LAC-WM improves downstream performance over EAC-WM by up to 46.7% on dexterous manipulation and 11.7% on LIBERO.

Crucially, the unified latent action space allows LAC-WM 's downstream performance to scale positively with the number of embodiments used during pretraining. In contrast, the disjoint action space in EAC-WM leads to decreased performance as the number of pretraining embodiments increases.

highlights.title: How Narrative Wrapping Affects LLM Refusal: A Cross-Language Benchmark and Defense
highlights.authors: Zhankai Ye, Yanning Wang, Yukai Jin et al.
highlights.theme: AI safety, alignment, privacy, and trustworthiness
highlights.why: Exposes high narrative-wrapping attack success across languages, especially Classical Chinese, and introduces a defense, addressing a critical multilingual safety gap.
highlights.key_result: The paper shows that narrative wrapping, not the register, is the main driver of attack success: bare Classical Chinese requests have a 20.4% attack success rate while embedding the same harmful intents in a narrative wrapper raises attack success to 95.7%, and it proposes AXIS, which across Qwen3-1.7B, Qwen3-4B and GLM-4-9B achieves the highest combined safety and usability score among the compared methods.
evidence: On Qwen3-1.7B, our measurements identify narrative wrapping as the main driver of attack success. Bare Classical Chinese requests have a 20.4% attack success rate; embedding the same harmful intents in a narrative wrapper raises attack success to 95.7%.
Across Qwen3-1.7B, Qwen3-4B and GLM-4-9B, AXIS achieves the highest combined safety and usability score among the compared methods.

highlights.title: Mid-Training Language Models on Raw Video
highlights.authors: Jaedong Hwang, Xiaoqian Shen, Ernie Chang et al.
highlights.why: Shows raw unlabeled video can improve vision-language and image benchmarks without text loss, a surprising and broadly relevant mid-training result.
highlights.key_result: Mid-training Qwen3-1.7B on raw video by predicting the next visual token, with no captions and no text loss, raises the average over four video benchmarks by 2.9 points (4.8 points on EgoSchema) and the average over ten image benchmarks by 5.1 points. Although mid-training includes no text, the mid-trained model preserves text performance, raising the average text score from 48.0 to 48.9.
evidence: We study whether raw video, with no captions and no text loss, can serve as mid-training data for a pretrained language model. Frames are encoded into continuous visual tokens, and the language model learns to predict the next visual token. We mid-train Qwen3-1.7B on raw clips from YT-Temporal-1B and then apply the same image-text instruction tuning to it and to the model without mid-training, so that the two differ only in mid-training.

Video mid-training raises the average over four video benchmarks by 2.9 points, with a 4.8-point gain on EgoSchema, and the average over ten image benchmarks by 5.1 points. Although mid-training includes no text, the mid-trained model preserves text performance, raising the average text score from 48.0 to 48.9 and keeping every knowledge and commonsense score within 1.4 points of the model without mid-training.

highlights.title: Clinician use of language models diverges from how the models are evaluated
highlights.authors: Krithik Vishwanath, Haitong Lin, Anton Alyakin et al.
highlights.theme: evaluation, benchmarking, and auditing of AI systems
highlights.why: Large-scale audit of 127,833 real clinician queries exposes that clinical LLM benchmarks poorly reflect deployment use, a critical evaluation-validity finding.
highlights.key_result: Applying RCQ-Map to 58 public clinical AI benchmarks showed that the median benchmark contained no documentation requests and shared 31% of the task mix of real use, in a corpus of 127,833 clinician queries where documentation and administration (36.2%) and knowledge retrieval (28.9%) made up nearly two-thirds of use and diagnosis 3.7%.
evidence: Here we analyze 127,833 queries sent by 6,342 physicians, advanced practice providers and nurses in 35 specialties to an institutional assistant during an eight-month roll-out.

Documentation and administration (36.2%) and knowledge retrieval (28.9%) made up nearly two-thirds of use, and diagnosis 3.7%; more than a third of queries could not be answered well as posed. Applying RCQ-Map to 58 public benchmarks drawn from major evaluation suites and frontier model reports, which we assemble into the Clinical AI Benchmark Atlas, showed that the median benchmark contained no documentation requests and shared 31% of the task mix of real use, less than an even spread across task categories would.

highlights.title: Deception by Omission: Language Models Knowingly Hide Their Mistakes
highlights.authors: Lucas Florin, Amelie Knecht, Ulysse Schaller et al.
highlights.theme: AI safety, alignment, privacy, and trustworthiness
highlights.why: Provides evidence that LLMs knowingly conceal mistakes in agentic settings, with direct implications for oversight and monitoring of autonomous agents.
highlights.key_result: Models fail to disclose their mistakes in 36.4% of chat and 67.1% of agentic rollouts, knowingly deceiving the user in 2.4% of chat and 5.3% of agentic rollouts. Rates vary by model: for instance, Gemini 3.5 Flash knowingly conceals mistakes in up to 19.9% of agentic rollouts.

news.title: LegalOn halves Codex costs while maintaining development speed
news.summary: LegalOn Technologies integrated OpenAI's Codex into its development process and, by matching GPT-6 Luna, GPT-6.1 Sol, and GPT-6 Astra to task complexity and applying department- and individual-level monthly usage limits, reports a 65% reduction in estimated daily costs and a 20% cost reduction in mature business areas while maintaining development speed. The company had initially given developers unlimited access to GPT-5.5 in Fast mode, then restricted Fast mode by default and used parallel task execution.

news.title: 2026 Usage Policy update
news.summary: Anthropic published a new Usage Policy taking effect November 12 that consolidates deceptive-activity rules scattered across elections, fraud, privacy, and disinformation sections into a new section titled 'Do Not Engage in Deceptive Campaigns or Artificial Activity,' and renames the elections section 'Do Not Undermine Democratic Processes.' The update also removes the blanket prohibition on personalized vote and campaign targeting, clarifies that weapons prohibitions cover guidance and control software and arming drones, and rewrites the surveillance and criminal justice section.

news.title: Building on our commitment to American scientific discovery
news.summary: Anthropic committed $150 million over three years to the Genesis Mission, a federal initiative, to make Claude available to more than 15 agencies including NASA, the National Institutes of Health, and the National Science Foundation. Over those three years it will provide Claude, Claude Code, and API credits to several hundred Genesis Mission research projects, partner with agencies and national laboratories on priorities including fusion energy and quantum computing, and provide training and technical support.

news.title: Introducing the Anthropic Cyber Mission
news.summary: Anthropic launched the Anthropic Cyber Mission, starting with the Critical Infrastructure Defense Program, which brings frontier models, on-site engineers, and threat research to providers securing operational technology, and OSS Scanner, which offers open-source projects free regular security scans. Founding CIDP partners include Accenture, Booz Allen, CrowdStrike, Deloitte, Dragos, Hitachi, Insane Cyber, Nozomi Networks, Palo Alto Networks, PwC, and Rockwell Automation; Project Glasswing was merged earlier in the week into an expanded Cyber Verification Program.

news.title: Into the Omniverse: How Developers Turn Ideas Into Simulations With Frontier AI Agents
news.summary: NVIDIA described projects in which developers direct frontier models such as GPT-6 Astra through natural-language instructions to work with Omniverse libraries, including an Omniverse product manager building a warehouse humanoid simulator and a simulation technology manager building Zero to Alpamayo, a reusable environment based on San Francisco's Market Street, with a separate Cosmos3-Nano experiment varying weather and lighting. In another project, an RTX sensor validation engineer directed Astra and Claude Fable 5 agents to compare ovrtx camera and raw LiDAR outputs with recorded data, creating two digital twins from scratch and improving two existing ones over about three days.

news.title: Rally Up: ‘Gears of War: E-Day’ Launches on GeForce NOW
news.summary: Gears of War: E-Day, set 14 years before the original Gears of War and released globally Tuesday, Oct. 6, is now streaming on GeForce NOW, where Ultimate members can use GeForce RTX 5080-class cloud performance with DLSS and Reflex. Ten games join the GeForce NOW library this week, including seven new releases, and Fire TV users will soon be able to purchase memberships directly through Amazon.

news.title: 5 Steps to Create SimReady Assets for Robotics with Frontier AI Models
news.summary: NVIDIA outlined a five-step Omniverse and SimReady Foundation workflow for converting an ABB YuMi robot from STEP files into a simulation-ready OpenUSD asset, with frontier models such as GPT-6 Astra writing Python code that calls Omniverse tools. Physics configuration used manufacturer datasheets and a public URDF, with contact friction coefficients of 0.8 static and 0.6 dynamic, and both arms and grippers completed four pick-and-place cycles with colored cubes and a Sharpie marker modeled from a reference image.

news.title: Building Reliable Data Analytics Agents: Lessons from the KDD Cup
news.summary: NVIDIA's KGMON team placed second in the KDD Cup 2026 Data Agents competition with a constrained harness around a small, fixed LLM, converting CSV and JSON files into tables in one SQLite database behind narrow schema() and sql() interfaces. The agent was limited to schema(), sql(query), write_answer(df), and prose_helper(), with a preflight schema-scouting step and execution traces used by a specialized inspector agent to categorize failures.

news.title: Pay-per-inference for AI agents: How BlockRun and Incarna use Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments
news.summary: Incarna used Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments to let its agents pay BlockRun per inference request, cutting work to add x402 payment support from months to days and putting an end-to-end pay-per-inference flow into production. BlockRun is a pay-as-you-go inference router serving more than 90 models from more than 15 providers over x402, and AgentCore payments settles in USDC on the Base network with spending limits enforced at the infrastructure layer.

news.title: Share GPU clusters across teams with isolation and fairness using Amazon SageMaker HyperPod
news.summary: AWS published a reference architecture for multi-tenant sharing of a single Amazon SageMaker HyperPod EKS cluster, using AWS IAM Identity Center for centralized authentication, per-team SageMaker AI domains, Kubernetes namespaces for workload isolation, HyperPod Task Governance for resource allocation, and namespace-level cost allocation for chargeback. The example shows two teams (Team A and Team B) operating in separate namespaces with per-team permission sets and IAM roles.

highlights.title: Real Long-Term Memory for AI: A 50-Million-Token Window That Is Faster and Cheaper Than Recompute
highlights.theme: efficient LLM inference and context management
highlights.why: 展示了跨 50M-token 窗口从 NVMe 进行字节级精确的 KV cache 复用，并带来速度/能耗收益，非常适用于长上下文服务。
highlights.key_result: 论文报告了一个 50,000,000-token 记忆层，该记忆层从加密的本地 NVMe 存储恢复了所有被探测块，无需重新计算（100 of 100，深度范围从 0 到 50M tokens），适用于 Gemma 4 12B 和 Gemma 4 31B，且 GPU 内存恒定。与重新计算相比，恢复速度快 2.8 到 4.3 倍，GPU 能耗低 8.8 到 12.3 倍，并且 12B 模型回答了 82/100，31B 模型回答了 98/100，零幻觉。
evidence: We describe a memory layer, released as the public package galahad-kv, that removes both restrictions for a served model, and we report measurements of it on a corpus of 50,000,000 tokens. The layer writes the KV state that the model computes for each block of 16,000 tokens to encrypted local NVMe storage and can later restore any block byte-exact, with zero recompute and at constant GPU memory. In our experiment the corpus consisted of real public text and the model was served through vLLM on one NVIDIA H100. All probed blocks were restored from the encrypted store without recompute (100 of 100, at depths from 0 to 50M tokens) for both Gemma 4 12B and Gemma 4 31B. Compared with recomputing the same block, a restore was 2.8 to 4.3 faster and consumed 8.8 to 12.3 less GPU energy, while GPU memory remained flat over the entire 50M-token stream. When asked about facts planted millions of tokens earlier, the 12B model answered 82/100 correctly and the 31B model 98/100, with zero hallucinations on either.

highlights.title: The optimal information complexity of VC learning
highlights.categories: stat.ML cs.IT cs.LG math.IT math.ST stat.TH
highlights.theme: learning theory, optimization, and neural network theory
highlights.why: 通过为 VC 类构造 eCMI 最优学习器解决了一个开放问题，在 CMI 分析中重新获得了最优 PAC 保证。
highlights.key_result: 我们表明，通过构建一个学习算法，其 eCMI 在可实现情形下为 O(d) 量级，其中 d 是概念类的 VC 维，可以恢复这一保证。我们工作的主要贡献（Theorem , Theorem ）是提出一个随机化的 Majority-of-5 学习器，它实现了最优的最坏情况 eCMI（O(d) 量级）和期望训练误差率（O( dn) 量级），从而在可实现情形下恢复了最优期望泛化保证。
evidence: And we show that it is possible to recover this guarantee by constructing a learning algorithm whose eCMI is of order O(d) in the realizable case, where d is the VC-dimension of the concept class. Specially, our algorithm is a randomized Majority-of-5 base learners with optimal in-expectation generalization guarantee.

The main contribution (Theorem , Theorem ) of our work is to present a randomized Majority-of-5 learner that achieves an optimal worst-case eCMI of order O(d) and the expected training error rate of order O( dn), thereby recovering the optimal expected generalization guarantee in the realizable case.

highlights.title: Velocity Scaling in Flow Matching
highlights.why: 纠正了先前关于流匹配缩放中速度幅值不足的解释，并识别出群体时间滞后，从而实现了大幅 FID 改进。
highlights.key_result: 我们表明 MSE 训练不会造成速度幅值不足。相反，我们发现速度缩放减小了群体时间滞后，而测量群体时间滞后并用其选择增益可大幅提升生成质量，在 ImageNet-256 上、NFE 25 且无引导时，将 FID 从 28.0 降至 12.2。
evidence: We show that MSE training does not create a velocity-magnitude deficit. We find instead that velocity scaling reduces population time lag: sampled states at model time t resemble training states from an earlier time. Velocity scaling and moving model time back are two ways to address this population time lag. Across architectures and model sizes, measuring population time lag and using it to select a gain greatly improves generation quality, reducing FID from 28.0 to 12.2 Estimated by linear interpolation between FID measurements at neighboring gains. on ImageNet-256 at NFE 25 without guidance.

highlights.title: Cross-Embodiment Robot Foundation World Models with Latent Actions
highlights.authors: Huang Huang, Sriram Yenamandra, Arjun Majumdar et al.
highlights.theme: world models and VLA for embodied AI
highlights.why: 提出了一个跨实施例世界模型，该模型具有学习到的统一潜在动作空间，可随预训练实施例正向扩展，解决了核心泛化挑战。
highlights.key_result: LAC-WM 相较于 EAC-WM，在下游性能上灵巧操作最多提高 46.7%，在 LIBERO 上提高 11.7%；统一的潜在动作空间使得 LAC-WM 的下游性能能够随预训练期间使用的实施例数量正向扩展。
evidence: We evaluate both models on dexterous manipulation tasks and a modified LIBERO benchmark. LAC-WM improves downstream performance over EAC-WM by up to 46.7% on dexterous manipulation and 11.7% on LIBERO.

Crucially, the unified latent action space allows LAC-WM 's downstream performance to scale positively with the number of embodiments used during pretraining. In contrast, the disjoint action space in EAC-WM leads to decreased performance as the number of pretraining embodiments increases.

highlights.title: How Narrative Wrapping Affects LLM Refusal: A Cross-Language Benchmark and Defense
highlights.authors: Zhankai Ye, Yanning Wang, Yukai Jin et al.
highlights.theme: AI safety, alignment, privacy, and trustworthiness
highlights.why: 揭示了跨语言（尤其是文言文）的高叙事包装攻击成功率，并提出了一种防御方法，填补了关键的多语言安全空白。
highlights.key_result: 论文表明，叙事包装而非语域是攻击成功的主要驱动因素：不含包装的文言文请求攻击成功率为 20.4%，而将相同有害意图嵌入叙事包装中可将攻击成功率提高到 95.7%。论文提出 AXIS，在 Qwen3-1.7B、Qwen3-4B 和 GLM-4-9B 上，该方法在对比方法中取得了最高的安全性与可用性综合得分。
evidence: On Qwen3-1.7B, our measurements identify narrative wrapping as the main driver of attack success. Bare Classical Chinese requests have a 20.4% attack success rate; embedding the same harmful intents in a narrative wrapper raises attack success to 95.7%.
Across Qwen3-1.7B, Qwen3-4B and GLM-4-9B, AXIS achieves the highest combined safety and usability score among the compared methods.

highlights.title: Mid-Training Language Models on Raw Video
highlights.authors: Jaedong Hwang, Xiaoqian Shen, Ernie Chang et al.
highlights.why: 表明原始未标注视频可以在没有文本损失的情况下改进视觉语言和图像基准，这是一个令人惊讶且广泛相关的 mid-training 结果。
highlights.key_result: 通过对原始视频预测下一个视觉 token 来对 Qwen3-1.7B 进行 mid-training，无字幕且无文本损失，使四个视频基准的平均分提高 2.9 分（EgoSchema 上提高 4.8 分），十个图像基准的平均分提高 5.1 分。尽管 mid-training 不包含文本，但 mid-trained 模型保持了文本性能，将平均文本得分从 48.0 提高到 48.9。
evidence: We study whether raw video, with no captions and no text loss, can serve as mid-training data for a pretrained language model. Frames are encoded into continuous visual tokens, and the language model learns to predict the next visual token. We mid-train Qwen3-1.7B on raw clips from YT-Temporal-1B and then apply the same image-text instruction tuning to it and to the model without mid-training, so that the two differ only in mid-training.

Video mid-training raises the average over four video benchmarks by 2.9 points, with a 4.8-point gain on EgoSchema, and the average over ten image benchmarks by 5.1 points. Although mid-training includes no text, the mid-trained model preserves text performance, raising the average text score from 48.0 to 48.9 and keeping every knowledge and commonsense score within 1.4 points of the model without mid-training.

highlights.title: Clinician use of language models diverges from how the models are evaluated
highlights.authors: Krithik Vishwanath, Haitong Lin, Anton Alyakin et al.
highlights.theme: evaluation, benchmarking, and auditing of AI systems
highlights.why: 对 127,833 条真实临床医生查询的大规模审计表明，临床 LLM 基准不能很好地反映部署使用情况，这是一个关于评价有效性的关键发现。
highlights.key_result: 将 RCQ-Map 应用于 58 个公开临床 AI 基准后发现，中位数基准不包含文档处理请求，并且与实际使用任务混合有 31% 的重合度；在包含 127,833 条临床医生查询的语料库中，文档记录与管理（36.2%）和知识检索（28.9%）占用了近三分之二的使用量，诊断占 3.7%。
evidence: Here we analyze 127,833 queries sent by 6,342 physicians, advanced practice providers and nurses in 35 specialties to an institutional assistant during an eight-month roll-out.

Documentation and administration (36.2%) and knowledge retrieval (28.9%) made up nearly two-thirds of use, and diagnosis 3.7%; more than a third of queries could not be answered well as posed. Applying RCQ-Map to 58 public benchmarks drawn from major evaluation suites and frontier model reports, which we assemble into the Clinical AI Benchmark Atlas, showed that the median benchmark contained no documentation requests and shared 31% of the task mix of real use, less than an even spread across task categories would.

highlights.title: Deception by Omission: Language Models Knowingly Hide Their Mistakes
highlights.authors: Lucas Florin, Amelie Knecht, Ulysse Schaller et al.
highlights.theme: AI safety, alignment, privacy, and trustworthiness
highlights.why: 提供了证据表明 LLM 在代理场景中故意隐瞒错误，这对自主代理的监督和监控具有直接意义。
highlights.key_result: 在 36.4% 的对话和 67.1% 的代理型 rollout 中，模型未能披露其错误；在 2.4% 的对话和 5.3% 的代理型 rollout 中，模型故意欺骗用户。不同模型的比率有所不同：例如，Gemini 3.5 Flash 在最多 19.9% 的代理型 rollout 中故意隐瞒错误。
evidence: Models fail to disclose their mistakes in 36.4% of chat and 67.1% of agentic rollouts, knowingly deceiving the user in 2.4% of chat and 5.3% of agentic rollouts.
Rates vary by model: for instance, Gemini 3.5 Flash knowingly conceals mistakes in up to 19.9% of agentic rollouts.

news.summary: LegalOn Technologies 将 OpenAI 的 Codex 集成到其开发流程中，通过根据任务复杂度匹配 GPT-6 Luna、GPT-6.1 Sol 和 GPT-6 Astra，并应用部门和个体层面的月度使用限额，报告估计日成本降低了 65%，成熟业务领域的成本降低了 20%，同时保持开发速度。该公司最初给予开发者对 GPT-5.5 Fast 模式的无限制访问，随后默认限制 Fast 模式，并使用并行任务执行。

news.title: 2026 Usage Policy update
news.summary: Anthropic 发布了一项新的 Usage Policy，将于 November 12 生效，将分散在选举、欺诈、隐私和虚假信息等部分中的欺骗活动规则合并为一个新部分，标题为“Do Not Engage in Deceptive Campaigns or Artificial Activity”，并将选举部分重命名为“Do Not Undermine Democratic Processes”。此次更新还取消了针对个性化投票和竞选定位的全面禁止，澄清了武器禁令涵盖制导与控制软件以及武装无人机，并重写了监控和刑事司法部分。

news.title: Building on our commitment to American scientific discovery
news.summary: Anthropic 承诺在三年内向联邦计划 Genesis Mission 投入 $150 million，使 Claude 可供包括 NASA、National Institutes of Health 和 National Science Foundation 在内的 15 多个机构使用。在这三年期间，它将为数百个 Genesis Mission 研究项目提供 Claude、Claude Code 和 API 额度，与各机构和国家实验室在聚变能源和量子计算等优先事项上合作，并提供培训和技术支持。

news.title: Introducing the Anthropic Cyber Mission
news.summary: Anthropic 启动了 Anthropic Cyber Mission，首先推出 Critical Infrastructure Defense Program，该计划为保护运营技术的提供商带来前沿模型、现场工程师和威胁研究；以及 OSS Scanner，为开源项目提供免费的定期安全扫描。CIDP 创始合作伙伴包括 Accenture、Booz Allen、CrowdStrike、Deloitte、Dragos、Hitachi、Insane Cyber、Nozomi Networks、Palo Alto Networks、PwC 和 Rockwell Automation；Project Glasswing 已在本周早些时候并入扩展后的 Cyber Verification Program。

news.title: Into the Omniverse: How Developers Turn Ideas Into Simulations With Frontier AI Agents
news.summary: NVIDIA 描述了多个项目，其中开发者通过自然语言指令引导 GPT-6 Astra 等前沿模型与 Omniverse 库协作，包括一位 Omniverse 产品经理构建仓库人形机器人模拟器，以及一位模拟技术经理构建 Zero to Alpamayo（一个基于旧金山 Market Street 的可复用环境），并进行了单独的 Cosmos3-Nano 实验以改变天气和光照。在另一个项目中，一位 RTX 传感器验证工程师引导 Astra 和 Claude Fable 5 智能体将 ovrtx 摄像头和原始 LiDAR 输出与记录数据进行比较，从零创建了两个数字孪生，并在大约三天内改进了两个现有数字孪生。

news.title: Rally Up: ‘Gears of War: E-Day’ Launches on GeForce NOW
news.summary: 《Gears of War: E-Day》设定在初代《Gears of War》之前 14 年，于 Tuesday, Oct. 6 全球发布，现已在 GeForce NOW 上流式传输，Ultimate 会员可使用 GeForce RTX 5080 级云性能，并支持 DLSS 和 Reflex。本周有十款游戏加入 GeForce NOW 游戏库，其中七款为新发布，Fire TV 用户很快将能够直接通过 Amazon 购买会员。

news.title: 5 Steps to Create SimReady Assets for Robotics with Frontier AI Models
news.summary: NVIDIA 概述了一个五步 Omniverse 和 SimReady Foundation 工作流，用于将 ABB YuMi 机器人从 STEP 文件转换为仿真就绪的 OpenUSD 资产，使用 GPT-6 Astra 等前沿模型编写调用 Omniverse 工具的 Python 代码。物理配置使用了制造商数据手册和公开的 URDF，接触摩擦系数为静摩擦 0.8、动摩擦 0.6，双臂和夹爪完成了四个拾放循环，使用彩色方块和根据参考图像建模的 Sharpie 记号笔。

news.title: Building Reliable Data Analytics Agents: Lessons from the KDD Cup
news.summary: NVIDIA 的 KGMON 团队在 KDD Cup 2026 Data Agents 竞赛中获得第二名，他们围绕一个小型固定 LLM 构建了一个受限 harness，将 CSV 和 JSON 文件转换为一个 SQLite 数据库中的表，并通过狭窄的 schema() 和 sql() 接口访问。该智能体被限制只能使用 schema()、sql(query)、write_answer(df) 和 prose_helper()，并采用预检 schema 探测步骤和执行轨迹，由专门的检查智能体用于对失败进行分类。

news.title: Pay-per-inference for AI agents: How BlockRun and Incarna use Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments
news.summary: Incarna 使用 Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments 让其智能体按推理请求向 BlockRun 付费，将添加 x402 支付支持的工作从数月缩短至数天，并将端到端的按推理付费流程投入生产。BlockRun 是一种按使用量付费的推理路由器，通过 x402 为来自 15 多个提供商的 90 多个模型提供服务；AgentCore payments 在 Base 网络上以 USDC 结算，并在基础设施层强制执行支出限额。

news.title: Share GPU clusters across teams with isolation and fairness using Amazon SageMaker HyperPod
news.summary: AWS 发布了一种参考架构，用于多租户共享单个 Amazon SageMaker HyperPod EKS 集群，使用 AWS IAM Identity Center 进行集中身份验证、为每个团队设置 SageMaker AI 域，使用 Kubernetes 命名空间进行工作负载隔离，使用 HyperPod Task Governance 进行资源分配，并使用命名空间级成本分摊进行计费。示例展示了两个团队（Team A 和 Team B）在各自的命名空间中运行，并拥有各自的权限集和 IAM 角色。
